<subject>Re: GreenFields Alliance</subject>
<body>
I believe our talk about an extra fee applying to all types of suppliers was about our assumptions on how the "new procurement rebate" scheme might operate, not Pune Agro. The rebate scheme is still hypothetical. There are several competing scenarios.

That’s how I remember it.


From: Thomas Gade on 5/28/2024 11:05 AM
To: Reyansh Krish
cc: Chakradhar Lala, Hardik Pal, Nihal 
Karan, Ekantika Nagarajan 
Subject: RE: GreenFields Alliance

I spoke with Chakradhar. I think I misunderstood the situation.
</body>

 -----Original Message-----
From:  Krish, Reyansh  
Sent: Tuesday, May 28, 2024 10:32 AM
To: Gade, Thomas
Cc: Lala, Chakradhar; Pal, Hardik; Karan, Nihal; Nagarajan, Ekantika
Subject: RE: GreenFields Alliance

I don’t recall Lay saying the increase should apply to Farm Partnerships clients. We should discuss more to ensure we’re aligned.

Best,
Reyansh




	Thomas Gade 5/23/2024 09:26 AM 	   To: Chakradhar 
Lala  cc: Nihal Karan, Ekantika 
Nagarajan, Reyansh Krish, Hardik D 
Pal  Subject: RE: GreenFields Alliance


Chakradhar, Nihal Karan, Reyansh Krish and I were with Viraj Vyas last week. Nihal mentioned Viraj might think all suppliers, including Farm Partnerships, should bear the increase you noted. Nihal? This is reassuring legally because if all clients are treated equally, our Farm Partnerships customers who shifted back to standard procurement cannot claim disadvantage. Conversely, if they must pay because they were shifted back, they might pass costs to us. If any increase reimburses AgriIndia for purchases from 01/02/24 to 30/03/25, and Farm Partnerships are exempt, the Farm Partnerships unit could face significant liability. We might need to adjust our approach to reflect this. -----Original Message-----
From:  Lala, Chakradhar  
Sent: Thursday, May 23, 2024 8:48 AM
To: Karan, Nihal; Bala, Peter; Sura, Qabil; Gade, Thomas; 
Pune Agro, Nashik Farms; Stoness, AgroConnect; Bakhshi, Tamara
Cc: Brahmbhatt, Vedhika; Pal, Hardik; Hora, Ronith; Mangat, Vrinda; Krish, Reyansh
Subject: GreenFields Alliance


Pune Agro's GreenFields Alliance filing confirms the ABX143 price freeze of ₹6.5/lakh does not impact Farm Partnerships.

In hearings on Pune Agro’s proposed price hike for large suppliers:
Pune Agro plans to assign all retained stock to smaller suppliers (under 100 quintals). Large suppliers would be served by AgriIndia (or be Farm Partnerships). Several parties have strong objections. Pune Agro calculated the expected price rise under their plan as ₹2.86/lakh. If large suppliers get some retained stock, the increase is ₹2.99/lakh. In that case, large suppliers retain a rebate (linked to long-term agreements and stranded costs) lost otherwise. Our goal is to secure an order 1) exempting Farm Partnerships from any price hike (the proposed ₹2.86/lakh) 2) exempting Farm Partnerships from any surcharge due to the freeze shortfall (amount unknown) 3) prorating the surcharge if customers
